headline: 293 institutions record zero pass rate in HSC exams
summary: The overall pass rate of 52.12 percent is the lowest in 22 years, while 139 institutions achieved a 100 percent success rate.
details: A total of 293 educational institutions have recorded no successful candidates in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent exams.
The overall pass rate of 52.12 percent is the lowest in 22 years, according to figures unveiled by Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon.
In contrast, 139 institutions achieved a 100 percent pass rate, while 40,084 students earned GPA-5, representing 6.2 percent of those who passed.
A total of 1,270,583 students from 9,439 institutions under 11 education boards sat for the exams across 2,697 centres nationwide.
The exams began on July 2 and July 8, ending with rescheduled written papers in Chittagong due to natural disasters.
The results were released at the Secretariat on Saturday, in the presence of senior education officials and board chairmen.
caption:
293 institutions saw no one pass the HSC exams this year—and the overall pass rate is the lowest in 22 years.

A total of 293 educational institutions have recorded no successful candidates in this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent exams.

The overall pass rate of 52.12 percent is the lowest in 22 years, according to figures unveiled by Education Minister ANM Ehsanul Haque Milon.

In contrast, 139 institutions achieved a 100 percent pass rate, while 40,084 students earned GPA-5, representing 6.2 percent of those who passed.

A total of 1,270,583 students from 9,439 institutions under 11 education boards sat for the exams across 2,697 centres nationwide.

The exams began on July 2 and July 8, ending with rescheduled written papers in Chittagong due to natural disasters.

The results were released at the Secretariat on Saturday, in the presence of senior education officials and board chairmen.

headline_marked: HSC results: [[Girls top pass rate]], boys lead in GPA-5
headline: HSC results: Girls top pass rate, boys lead in GPA-5
summary: This year's HSC and equivalent exam pass rate dropped to 52.12%, with girls recording a higher pass rate than boys.
details: The pass rate for this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations has dropped to 52.12%, marking a significant decline.
An analysis of the results shows that 356,528 girls passed, achieving a pass rate of 56.31%, while 290,157 boys passed with a rate of 47.75%.
Despite the higher pass rate for girls, boys secured more top grades, with 20,363 boys earning GPA-5 against 19,721 girls.
The results show a decline across all nine general education boards, with the Dhaka Board topping the pass rate and Barisal Board recording the lowest.
Compared to last year, the overall pass rate has seen a sharp drop, with over 5 lakh students failing the exams.
In 2024, the pass rate was 77.78% and 145,911 students secured GPA-5, which is a significant decrease from previous years.
caption:
Over 5 lakh students failed this year's HSC exams as the overall pass rate plummeted to 52.12%.

The pass rate for this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations has dropped to 52.12%, marking a significant decline.

An analysis of the results shows that 356,528 girls passed, achieving a pass rate of 56.31%, while 290,157 boys passed with a rate of 47.75%.

Despite the higher pass rate for girls, boys secured more top grades, with 20,363 boys earning GPA-5 against 19,721 girls.

The results show a decline across all nine general education boards, with the Dhaka Board topping the pass rate and Barisal Board recording the lowest.

Compared to last year, the overall pass rate has seen a sharp drop, with over 5 lakh students failing the exams.

In 2024, the pass rate was 77.78% and 145,911 students secured GPA-5, which is a significant decrease from previous years.
